strengths: Addresses an important question: what multimodal contrastive learning can recover when modalities have distinct, statistically coupled latent factors.
The inexpensive CLIP postprocessing pipeline reports improvements across four backbones, multiple shot counts, ImageNet distribution shifts, and 11 adaptation datasets.
Synthetic experiments include three repetitions and distributional misspecification tests. Appendix P adds quantitative ground-truth recovery on Multimodal3DIdent.
weaknesses: The central proof is invalid (Appendix D.1, Lemma 2). It claims that the normalized population loss has minimum 0, but under the spherical model with matched temperature, identity latent encoders achieve −2I(z_x;z_t)<0 for positive coupling. Furthermore, the vMF conditional has full support, so requiring equal embeddings almost surely for positive pairs forces constant representations, contradicting the simultaneous uniformity requirement. Both identifiability theorems depend on this lemma, leaving the main guarantees unestablished.

The convex-body proof has additional substantive problems. A uniform source marginal and a normalized distance kernel generally produce a nonuniform target marginal because of boundary effects. Lemma 3 concerns the limit λ→0, but Equation 43 uses uniformity as an exact equality without this restriction. Corollary 2 also omits the L_alpha, alpha≠2 restriction introduced in Appendix E.2; arbitrary norms can permit rotational ambiguity rather than permutation identifiability.

The ICA justification conflicts with the spherical assumptions. Cartesian coordinates of a continuously uniform hyperspherical variable are dependent, and its distribution is rotationally invariant. Consequently, FastICA cannot uniquely resolve the orthogonal mixing from this distribution. Adding independent-component assumptions is incompatible with the stated prior. The proposed PCA/local-isometry argument likewise does not establish that the convex-body guarantee applies to CLIP.

The experiments do not isolate disentanglement as the source of downstream improvements. FastICA includes dimensionality reduction and whitening, while the compared pipelines retain different numbers of components. Dimension-matched PCA-only and whitening-only controls are missing. In particular, an orthogonal rotation of the same whitened features cannot change the converged L2-regularized linear-probe optimum, making the whitening baseline essential.

The disentanglement evidence is insufficient for the component-wise claims. Selected CelebA traversals and counts of interpretable attributes lack controlled comparisons. Appendix P's R² scores assess linear predictability, rather than component-wise recovery or independence. Moreover, Appendix K fits learned representations from ground-truth factors; a rank-deficient linear representation can score perfectly under this evaluation without preserving all factors.

The 'beyond DAGs' contribution needs stronger justification. An undirected statistical dependence does not establish greater causal expressive power than a model with a latent regime variable. The analysis assumes a single specific coupling distribution, and the experiments do not test the motivating mixtures of opposing causal mechanisms. The final isometry arguments also substantially reuse Zimmermann et al. (2021).

Reproducibility and reporting remain incomplete: the data used to fit PCA/ICA and several training details are unclear, and the principal real-data comparisons lack uncertainty estimates. Table 2 also reports the RN101 baseline target average as 20.03, although its four entries average 22.025, overstating the apparent improvement.
